negative_controls.description: Same planted tree: guard refuses -A (index unchanged) AND raw git add -A on a twin scratch repo stages the sibling.
After scoped add+commit, inspect_index out_of_scope is [].
verify_cached=False allows a contaminated index; the live cached-vs-scope check refuses it.

notes: G-1 delivery of IMP-0428. Live named probes exit 0. Receipt state=SUCCESS. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok is not consulted. Scratch-repo git only; no add/commit/push/stash/checkout/rebase on the program worktree.
question_or_target: Implement the guard for concurrent agents sharing one git index: forbid broad staging, require a scoped path list, and verify the staged set against the unit's declared file scope before any commit is offered. Exact question: does a scoped stage plus a diff --cached check catch a sibling file that a broad add would have swept in?

residual_unknowns.claim: WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json has no structured declared_file_scope field today. Operational scope is the sidecar probes/IMP-0428/declared-scope.json plus output_path, and callers may pass an explicit list. Catalog prose inputs are not treated as path grants.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: When the catalog grows a declared_file_scope array, re-run load_declared_scope against every unit and require a non-empty fail-closed result without a sidecar.

residual_unknowns.claim: IMP-0410/IMP-0411 (advisory leases / overlap) are catalog dependencies and are not delivered on this tree. This guard does not consult leases; it only gates staging/commit-offer against a path scope.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Bind inspect_index to IMP-0411 overlap once that unit is live.

retry.policy: no automatic retry; a contaminated stage is surfaced to the orchestrator, never auto-corrected

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 is the security review of the refusal path: traversal, empty scope, commit -a, and a mutation that disables the cached-vs-scope check. It does not reuse probe 1's scratch repo.
